note: Forest Service campground at the end of Forest Road 1892, 12 miles south of Rolla, on Little Piney Creek, a wild trout stream. Shaded back-in sites under hardwoods (sites 4 and 13 pull through), each with a table, lantern post and fire ring; six sites have electric hookups. Six nonelectric sites, 8, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16, are next to the creek. Highway 63 traffic can sometimes be heard. --Claude
summary: FS page: open April 1 - October 31, 2026; $15 single, $25 electric, $30 double, $2 extra vehicle (2 included); campsites FCFS, only the pavilions reservable; 6 electric (1-5, 7), 11 nonelectric, 4 doubles = 21 sites, no water/sewer hookups, no amperage, no rig limit; creek sites 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 16 (21-43 m from the water) - creekside held. Electric 15 A and max_rig 34 removed (unsupported). Pin moved 240 m from across the creek to the Loop A centre. Phone 417-967-4194 to add.
flags: PIN: stored 37.7931,-91.8361 (the rec.gov facility point) is in woods on the SOUTH side of Little Piney Creek beside a pond, about 120 m across the creek from the campground and 240 m from the sites' centre. Move to 37.79517,-91.83533 (centroid of the 18 Loop A catalog sites). The FS page's own Getting There point is 37.796016,-91.835922 (by site 04).
PHONE: none stored. FS page 'Houston/Rolla/Cedar Creek Ranger District ... Phone: 417-967-4194'; rec.gov facility_phone '417-967-4194'. Suggest phone -> 417-967-4194.

WATERFRONT (creekside, held): the FS page names the creek sites: 'Six of the nonelectric sites are next to the Little Piney Creek, sites 8, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16.' Measured from the catalog's site coordinates to the near edge of the channel on leaf-off imagery: 08 ~35 m, 09 ~21-34 m, 11 ~38-43 m, 13 ~42 m, 15 ~25-31 m, 16 ~21-33 m - all inside 50 m. The ground between is open bottomland forest floor under the same scattered hardwoods as the sites; no road, parking or other developed strip shows between those six and the bank. Canopy (FS 'shaded'; catalog 'Shade: Full') keeps the imagery from confirming the bank height, so the agency's per-site statement is the deciding source. Site 07 is ~59 m and the rest farther. The catalog's 'Proximity to Water: Riverfront' is on all 23 units including the pavilions - a blanket tag, not evidence.

HOOKUPS: electric 15 A REMOVED. It came from the catalog's 'Electricity Hookup: 15', which is set on every unit - the 8 STANDARD NONELECTRIC sites, the 3 group nonelectric sites and both pavilions too - so it is a facility-wide template value, not a site amperage; the FS page states electric at 6 sites with no amperage. If AWH would rather keep 15, it is reversible. Water/sewer false per the FS page.

ELECTRIC SITE CONFLICT: FS page 'Single Electric: 6 sites - sites 1 through 5, and site 7'; the rec.gov catalog types 10 sites STANDARD ELECTRIC (01-07, 10, 12, 14). rec.gov doesn't sell these sites (all FCFS), so the FS count is used in the note; no field holds the count.

RIG LENGTH: max_rig_ft 34 REMOVED - it came from earlier sweep note prose and no source states a limit: the FS page gives none, and the catalog's Max Vehicle Length is 0 (blank) on every site. Driveways are 'Paved' per catalog; the FS page says most sites are back-ins, sites 4 and 13 pull through. Fit is unconfirmed but the paved back-in loop in a USFS family campground is not a fit concern on its face.

SITES: count 17 -> 21 (FS: 6 electric + 11 nonelectric + 4 doubles, which sums to sites 1-21; the catalog lists 01-21). Sites 19-21 are typed 'GROUP STANDARD NONELECTRIC' on rec.gov, but the FS page calls them doubles (16 people, $30).

SEASON: FS 'Campground Open April 1 - October 31, 2026' (day use March 1 - October 31); rec.gov maxStay rule dated 04-01 to 10-31; rec.gov 2026 Peak Season rates run 04-01 to 10-27. Season set manual; the 'Approximate' note removed.

CURRENT CONDITIONS (FS page): 'Please bring your own water if you are visiting Lane Springs Recreation Area between now and the end of October. A routine inspection found several leaks in the water system, requiring the system be shut down until it can be repaired.' The page lists water spigots, but its amenity block says 'Potable water is not available at this site.' facilities.potable_water left unset rather than recording a temporary outage either way.
ALERTS: the Mark Twain alerts list (Paddy Creek bridge replacement, Trail 119, Beaver Lake, Red Bridge Road bridge) has nothing for Forest Road 1892 or Lane Spring.

OPERATOR: Forest Service (Houston/Rolla/Cedar Creek Ranger District), fees at the fee tube, on-site host; no concessionaire named. FCFS for all 21 campsites; only the Dogwood and Redbud pavilions are reservable on rec.gov.
FEES: double $30 put in fees.note rather than nightly_high (nightly_low/high = single sites $15/$25). Day use $5 per vehicle not recorded.
